subject: toucan
reasoning:
I'm planning the toucan's proportions and coloring—standing posture around 0.45m tall, a large colorful beak roughly 0.18m with orange, yellow, red and black patches, plus the distinctive black body, white bib, and blue eye markings.

Now I'm laying out the skeleton: hips as the root joint positioned low, with a spine chain curving upward and forward through chest to neck base using a catmull path, keeping the body tilted upright like a perched toucan while the tail sweeps back and down separately.

I'm continuing to build out the neck and head joints, deciding to split the head into its own separate joint rather than letting it be the tip of the neck chain, so I can control its facing direction forward instead of just following the path's tangent.

Now I'm working out the body sweep, shaping the torso as an elliptical loft along the spine chain with radii tapering from front to back, then planning a separate, thinner sweep along the neck chain, with body colored black to start matching toucan markings.

For the throat and chest markings, I'm deciding to use angular sectors on the neck and upper body tube to paint a bib region, or alternatively stick a flattened sphere decal onto the front of the chest for simplicity. I'll keep the head as its own sphere part — black crown, with the white/yellow throat achieved via a stuck-on sphere toward the lower front.

Still placing anatomy pieces...

Planning the beak shape with a loft along curved stations, tapering width and height as it extends forward and curves downward toward the tip.

For coloring I'm thinking of using position-based paint logic rather than a flat color — going for a keel-billed toucan look with banded colors along the beak's length: yellow near the base, transitioning to orange, then red at the tip.

Now I'm setting up the lower mandible as a separate jaw piece, jointed to the head and lofted through a series of stations tapering toward the tip, using the same bone-based loft approach as the upper beak.

For the wing, I'm figuring out how to extrude the folded wing shape against the body's tilt, aligning its axis so it lies backward and down from the shoulder, matching the body's natural up-forward angle.

I'm setting up a local coordinate system for the wing, with one axis running along its length toward the tail and the other across its width toward the trailing edge, so I can plot the outline points for the leading and trailing edges.

Working out wing bone attachment...

I'll name the joints wingL/wingR per side, then add a darker feather overlay color for contrast against the body black. For the tail, I'm sketching a backward-downward chain of points from the hips.

Now I'm adding red undertail coverts as a scaled sphere near the hip joint, positioned to poke out slightly from under the body's rear sweep where the radius narrows.

For the rump I'm placing a small pale yellow-white sphere at the upper tail coverts for a subtle banding effect. Then I'm setting up short bluish-gray legs using a limb chain from hip to foot with bent knee joints, and planning zygodactyl feet with two toes forward and two back as small rod shapes.

Writing toe joints and rods...

Positioning the toes and leg tip geometry, then thinking about small beak details like the nostril and tip coloring before deciding to keep the body paint simple with a subtle dark blue-black sheen rather than added countershading.

Now I'm working out the color sectoring for the toucan's bib and belly: black as the base with a defined patch for the white/yellow bib on the neck and chest, transitioning to black belly and red undertail further back, using angular sectors and a t-range along the body spine to position the bib correctly. I'm setting the neck radius and head sphere placement so the throat sphere blends smoothly into the bib region.

Settling on a belly radius function that bulges slightly using a sine curve, giving it a thicker midsection. For the wings, placing them at x±0.09 with the inner face just inside the body surface so they sit flush against the torso. Now moving on to figuring out foot positions.

Checking the overall height scale lands around 0.5-0.53, which seems plausible once the beak length is included. For the eyes, considering adding the orange/blue skin ring typical of toucans around the eye socket, then placing a small pupil sphere offset outward and flattened in one axis to sit naturally within that ring.

Working through exact coordinates so the eye ring and pupil protrude slightly from the head sphere's surface without floating or sinking in -- adjusting the ring's x-position and scale so it reaches the edge properly, and confirming the pupil sits a bit further out for visible depth. Also checking that the beak's base overlaps correctly with the front of the head sphere so there's no visible gap at the join.

Now I'm adding a jaw joint attached to the head, positioned slightly forward and down, with its aim pointing further forward for natural jaw movement.

I'm defining a paint function for the beak's coloring, splitting the upper and lower mandible into color bands by z-position -- green near the base transitioning to yellow, orange, and red toward the tip, with a special highlight color along the upper ridge. I'm also adding a thin black band right at the beak's base to visually separate it from the head.

Now I'm skipping the overlapping base detail and moving to the leg structure -- building a joint chain for hips, knees, and ankles, then sweeping capsule geometry along that chain for leg thickness. I'm attaching toe capsules to the leg's tip joint, and setting up the color palette with black, a pale bib tone, and a red accent.

For the wings, I'm placing a joint and extruding an outline for the main wing shape, then adding a second overlapping outline for covert feathers in a darker slate tone, offset slightly further out for a layered feather look.
